body.p: Seven audio features rescaled across all keys. Keys with a bold colored border scored at least 1σ above the median on one feature and earned a personality label.

div.div: Chromatic Scale, C4 → B4 (coloured by personality label)
8 of 12 keys have a clearly distinctive audio profile (z > 1σ above median on at least one feature). The remaining keys fall within the normal range. Read left to right, C through B.

div.span: ♫ Or Nah (feat. The Weeknd, Wiz Khalifa & DJ Mustard) - Remix

div.div: Groove champion: C♯/D♭ has the steadiest pulse of all 12 keys.
Vocals step aside in D, where ambient, lo-fi, and film scores dominate.
Pure sunshine: D♯/E♭ is the happiest-sounding key in the dataset.
E sounds like a live show, with more crowd noise, stage energy, and raw performance.

div.span: ♫ Kapoor & Sons Mashup (By DJ Chetas) (From "Kapoor & Sons (Since 1921)")

div.div: Vocals step aside in F♯/G♭, where ambient, lo-fi, and film scores dominate.
Vocals step aside in A, where ambient, lo-fi, and film scores dominate.
The wordiest key: A♯/B♭ is packed with rapping, storytelling, and spoken delivery.
B sounds like a live show, with more crowd noise, stage energy, and raw performance.

div.p: A key earns its personality when one audio feature is ≥ 1 standard deviation above the median (after min-max rescaling). Not every key has a personality; some are simply average across all features.

tr.td: These keys attract the most groove-friendly, steady-beat tracks. You'd hear them at a dance party.
Vocals are unusually absent. Favoured by ambient, classical, and lo-fi artists.
Recordings that capture the feel of a live performance. You can almost hear the crowd.
Word-heavy: rap, spoken word, storytelling. The vocals carry more than the melody.
The happiest keys. Music theory aside, these tracks just sound sunny.
